 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. India and New Zealand clash in the second of five ODIs in the series at Hnry Stadium, Wellington on Saturday, November 7. The Indians won the recent T20I series 3-2 despite the Kiwis managing to win the last two matches.
 The ODI series sees the comeback of Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli in the Indian squad, while Shubman Gill leads the team in the five ODIs. India lead the series 1-0 after a 5-wicket win in the opening game in Auckland.

 The home side is dealing with injury concerns as Devon Conway has been ruled out of the rest of the series, while Rachin Ravindra and Mark Chapman were previously ruled out. Weather might be a major factor in the upcoming game.
 The Sporting News takes a look at how the weather is expected to behave in Wellington for the second ODI between India and New Zealand.

 Wellington weather forecast for New Zealand vs. India 2nd ODI
 The weather report for Saturday looks concerning for the second match of the series, with overcast skies and spells of rain predicted in Wellington.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement According to the current forecast, there is a prediction of a high of about 19°C with temperatures remaining near 19°C around the start of the game. Heavy cloud cover sitting near 99 per cent alongside gusty winds is expected throughout the day. There is a prediction of temperatures dropping down to about 16°C by evening time.

 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Chances of rain interrupting play in Wellington
 There is a 60% chance of rain during the day on Saturday in Wellington, with weather threats peaking around the afternoon match hours.
 Persistent showers on Friday forced India to cancel their training session ahead of the match, highlighting the lingering wet conditions. Rain probabilities climb rapidly right around the afternoon start.
 The chances of rain during the playing time will hover between 50% and 60% during the initial hours. Although a clearer window might appear during the early evening, rising rain probabilities later in the night could lead to delays or stoppages.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement What happens if the New Zealand vs. India 2nd ODI is stopped by rain?
 If in any case rain interrupts play, the playing conditions can be adjusted to compensate for the loss of time.
 The Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) system will be applied to set a new target based on a reduction in the number of overs. First, the match officials will try to play as many overs as possible given the weather conditions and playing time. Under ODI conditions, both teams must face a minimum of 20 overs each for a official result to be declared.
 If it is not viable to bowl enough overs to get a result, the match will end in a no-result match.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Hnry Stadium pitch report and dew factor for IND vs NZ 2nd ODI
 Traditionally, the playing surface at Hnry Stadium (formerly Sky Stadium) offers help to fast bowlers early on due to the cool, windy conditions and high humidity levels in Wellington. Batters need to spend time settling in before capitalizing on the venue's unique boundaries.
 The seamers are expected to find significant assistance with the new ball under heavy overhead cloud cover, while spinners may come into play if the surface stays dry between rain breaks.
 Atmospheric moisture and cool evening temperatures could introduce a dew factor in the second innings under floodlights. Combined with potential rain interruptions, captains winning the toss are likely to favor fielding first.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement What time does the New Zealand vs. India 2nd ODI start?
 The second ODI between New Zealand and India will be played at Hnry Stadium in Wellington, New Zealand.
 It is scheduled to start at 3:00 p.m. local time (NZDT), which translates to 7:30 a.m. IST on Saturday, November 7 , for viewers in India .
